requirement: Export nested dataclass settings containing paths and enums as plain YAML that safe_load reads back, without registering representers on PyYAML's global SafeDumper.
skeleton: An empty SettingsDumper SafeDumper subclass, path and enum representer functions registered as multi-representers on it, and dump_settings validating an instance and dumping asdict in field order.
caption: Dumping dataclass settings to YAML with PyYAML by teaching a private SafeDumper subclass about paths and enums, never the global one. SettingsDumper is an empty yaml.SafeDumper subclass. Multi-representers registered on it alone turn any PurePath, including concrete PosixPath, into its posix string, and any Enum into the representation of its value, so an IntEnum stays an integer. dump_settings(settings) raises TypeError saying settings must be a dataclass instance for anything but a dataclass instance, including a dataclass class, and returns yaml.dump of dataclasses.asdict with that Dumper and sort_keys=False, so nested dataclasses become mappings. The fixture asserts the exact field-ordered output, a safe_load round trip, concrete paths, that global safe_dump still refuses enums and paths, and the dataclass instance check.

plan.intent: Export typed settings as readable YAML
constraints: Representers are registered only on the SettingsDumper subclass
PurePath subclasses dump as posix strings and enums as their values
Nested dataclasses are converted with dataclasses.asdict
Anything but a dataclass instance raises TypeError

rationale.teaches: Register add_multi_representer on a private SafeDumper subclass so subclasses like PosixPath match, represent enum values with represent_data, and dump asdict output.
rationale.why: add_representer matches only the exact class so real paths fail, registering on yaml.SafeDumper changes every safe_dump in the process, and vars leaves nested dataclasses unrepresentable.

ops.docstring: Dump dataclass settings through representers on a private SafeDumper.

ops.source:
class SettingsDumper(yaml.SafeDumper):  # pylint: disable=too-many-ancestors
    """A SafeDumper that also knows paths and enums."""

def _represent_path(dumper: SafeRepresenter, data: PurePath) -> Node:
    return dumper.represent_str(data.as_posix())

def _represent_enum(dumper: SafeRepresenter, data: Enum) -> Node:
    return dumper.represent_data(data.value)

candidates.why_wrong: add_representer matches only PurePath itself, so PosixPath values fail to dump.
The enum representer is registered on the global SafeDumper for every caller.
vars leaves nested dataclasses as objects that the dumper cannot represent.
A dataclass class is passed to asdict and fails with its own TypeError.
Integer enum values are dumped as quoted strings instead of numbers.
